package org.opentaint.dataflow.bidi.external

import org.opentaint.dataflow.ap.ifds.AccessPathBase
import org.opentaint.dataflow.bidi.ap.*
import org.opentaint.dataflow.bidi.fixtures.StoreFixtures
import org.opentaint.dataflow.bidi.store.DemandStore

private fun quote(s: String): String = "\"" + s.replace("\\", "\\\\").replace("\"", "\\\"") + "\""
private fun json(x: Any?): String = when (x) {
    null -> "null"
    is String -> quote(x)
    is Boolean, is Number -> x.toString()
    is Map<*, *> -> x.entries.joinToString(",", "{", "}") { quote(it.key.toString()) + ":" + json(it.value) }
    is Iterable<*> -> x.joinToString(",", "[", "]") { json(it) }
    else -> error("Unsupported JSON value: $x")
}
fun main() {
    val fixture = StoreFixtures()
    val ap = fixture.manager
    val ops = fixture.ops
    val method = fixture.method
    val x = AccessPathBase.Argument(0)
    val f = fixture.field("f")
    val g = fixture.field("g")
    val t = fixture.mark("T")
    val markT = MarkSlot.Concrete(t)
    val policy = RestrictedInitialPolicy(run = 5, fieldLimit = 4, direction = Direction.FORWARD)
    val cases = ArrayList<Map<String, Any?>>()
    fun pattern(path: List<Int>, tail: Tail, mark: MarkSlot) = fixture.pattern(x, path, tail, mark)
    fun describe(p: Pattern): Map<String, Any?> = linkedMapOf(
        "base" to p.fact.base.toString(), "path" to p.fact.path, "tail" to p.fact.tail.name,
        "mark" to (if (p.fact.mark is MarkSlot.Star) "FLOW" else "T"),
        "E" to (p.exclusion as? ExclusionSet.Concrete)?.ids?.toList().orEmpty(),
        "mx" to ((p.fact.mark as? MarkSlot.Star)?.excluded?.ids?.toList().orEmpty()))
    fun describe(a: AdmittedInitial): Map<String, Any?> = describe(a.initial.toPattern()) + ("layer" to a.layer.name)
    fun outputs(store: DemandStore, fact: Facts) = store.initials(method, fact, policy)
    fun store(entry: Pattern): DemandStore = DemandStore.Builder(ap).apply {
        check(add(method, DemandPattern(entry, null)))
    }.build()
    val broad = pattern(emptyList(), Tail.ANY, MarkSlot.STAR)
    val view = store(broad)
    fun packet(name: String, tail: Tail, layer: Layer) {
        val root = fixture.fact(x, tail = tail, mark = MarkSlot.STAR, layer = layer) as FlowTree
        val child = fixture.fact(x, listOf(f), tail, MarkSlot.STAR, layer = layer) as FlowTree
        val combined = ap.flowTree(x, layer, ExclusionSet.Empty, MarkExclusions.EMPTY,
            FlowAlgebra.mergeAdd(root.root, child.root, ap.cancellation), root.tail)
        check(ops.leaves(combined).count() == 2)
        val rootResult = outputs(view, root)
        val packetResult = outputs(view, combined)
        val rootLayer = if (root.tail == Tail.ANY) Layer.DEMAND else Layer.NORMAL
        val expectedRoot = AdmittedInitial(ap.initial(pattern(emptyList(), root.tail, MarkSlot.STAR)), rootLayer)
        val expectedChild = AdmittedInitial(ap.initial(pattern(listOf(f), Tail.STAR, MarkSlot.STAR)), Layer.NORMAL)
        check(rootResult == setOf(expectedRoot)) { "$name unexpected root: $rootResult" }
        check(packetResult == setOf(expectedRoot, expectedChild)) { "$name unexpected packet: $packetResult" }
        cases += linkedMapOf("name" to name, "entryDemand" to describe(broad),
            "requestedLayer" to layer.name, "requestedTail" to tail.name,
            "actualLayer" to root.layer.name, "actualTail" to root.tail.name,
            "rootOnlyLeaves" to ops.leaves(root).map { describe(Pattern(it.fact, it.exclusion)) }.toList(),
            "twoLeafPacketLeaves" to ops.leaves(combined).map { describe(Pattern(it.fact, it.exclusion)) }.toList(),
            "rootOnlyAdmitted" to rootResult.map { describe(it) },
            "twoLeafPacketAdmitted" to packetResult.map { describe(it) },
            "removedBySpatialMinimization" to (packetResult - rootResult).map { describe(it) },
            "setsEqual" to (rootResult == packetResult))
    }
    packet("MAY-FLOW-DEMAND-root-plus-f", Tail.ANY, Layer.DEMAND)
    packet("MUST-FLOW-NORMAL-root-plus-f", Tail.ANY_TAINT, Layer.NORMAL)
    packet("MUST-FLOW-DEMAND-abstract-intrinsic-layer-control", Tail.ANY_TAINT, Layer.DEMAND)
    val dc0 = pattern(emptyList(), Tail.ANY, markT)
    val dc1 = pattern(listOf(f), Tail.ANY, markT)
    for (layer in listOf(Layer.NORMAL, Layer.DEMAND)) {
        val actual = fixture.fact(x, listOf(f, g), Tail.EXACT, markT, layer = layer)
        val shallow = outputs(store(dc0), actual)
        val deeper = outputs(store(dc1), actual)
        check(shallow == setOf(AdmittedInitial(ap.initial(pattern(listOf(f), Tail.STAR, markT)), Layer.DEMAND)))
        check(deeper == setOf(AdmittedInitial(ap.initial(pattern(listOf(f, g), Tail.EXACT, markT)), layer)))
        cases += linkedMapOf("name" to "shallow-vs-deeper-MAY-demand-concrete-$layer",
            "actual" to ops.leaves(actual).map { describe(Pattern(it.fact, it.exclusion)) }.toList(),
            "actualLayer" to layer.name, "shallowDemand" to describe(dc0), "deeperDemand" to describe(dc1),
            "shallowAdmitted" to shallow.map { describe(it) }, "deeperAdmitted" to deeper.map { describe(it) },
            "setsEqual" to (shallow == deeper))
    }
    println(json(linkedMapOf("state" to "PASS", "runtimeRevision" to "52f32dd437d438aec4a700a02c18d94c31d58093",
        "policy" to linkedMapOf("run" to 5, "direction" to "FORWARD", "fieldLimit" to 4),
        "fieldIds" to linkedMapOf(f.toString() to "Box#f", g.toString() to "Box#g"),
        "markId" to t.id, "cases" to cases,
        "claim" to "Native DemandStore C2 differs after spatial MAY/MUST packet minimization and after descendant-demand deletion. Complete admitted initial patterns and layers are retained.")))
}

# MAY/MUST antichains and next-run demand pruning

Read-only design audit of measured runtime `52f32dd437d438aec4a700a02c18d94c31d58093`, using the new report `docs/reports/bidirectional-field-path-demand-witnesses-20261104.md` and the selected C2/C5 specification. The initial source audit was followed by five bounded native C2 controls using the existing compiled runtime (512 MiB, one CPU). No Gradle, project run, core/source change or newly selected policy. C5 examples below remain source-derived, not newly executed.

The main distinction is **spatial data coverage versus refinement-label coverage**. The observed packed-store leaks are real scalar-coverage gaps. Removing their labels before the next handoff is not automatically a native-behavior-preserving optimization. A leaked descendant can accidentally carry useful extra C2 refinement or a larger C5 output budget.

## 1. Current laws and where they are incomplete

The complete scope is: original method context, direction, complete premise P (including every ND member), block entry, exact exit, conclusion base, layer, kind, tail, field exclusion E, mark exclusion mx, and concrete protection. Roots and physical feedback/exception ports cannot mix.

| Store/cell | Current behavior | Remaining opportunity |
|---|---|---|
| `FlowGroup`, `ap/Groups.kt:14–79` | Separate layers. Same-path same-tail merge. Existing ANY leaf covers arriving descendant paths. STAR/EXACT/MUST only at the same path. | MUST proper-prefix scalar parity is missing. No minimization of ancestor+descendant leaves inside the offered DAG. A later broad arrival does not generally delete old descendants. |
| `TaintGroup`, `Groups.kt:102–190` | Uses scalar-style ANY/MUST proper-prefix subtraction against existing packets; protection is subtracted separately against protected coverage. | Does not inherently minimize one offered packet before comparing it with existing packets; broad-after-narrow can leave old descendants. |
| `DiagonalRelations`, `store/DiagonalRelations.kt:144–191,363–376` | Diagonal concrete STAR/ANY only; STAR exact-coordinate subtraction, ANY prefix subtraction. One geometry has mark/protection masks. | Incoming geometry is not internally prefix-minimized; no general deletion of all old covered geometry on broad insertion. MUST is not a supported packed diagonal header. |
| `FlowBackedCoverage.kt:39–57` | FLOW-to-concrete replacement only for STAR/ANY, same initial counterpart shape and matching output tails, with protected bits retained. | Extending this to MUST or mixing MAY/MUST/layers is a new proof obligation, not the same fix as FLOW packet minimization. |

Same-header data candidates, deliberately conservative:

```text
MAY:  at path p, an existing mark/flag covers the same flag at every p.r.
MUST: at path p/E, it covers a proper descendant p.r if E admits the descent;
      at equal paths, require E_source subset E_target.
STAR: preserve suffix correlation; no new ancestor-prefix rule.
EXACT: equal coordinate only.
```

For FLOW, require covering mx subset of covered mx. For concrete marks, cover only the actually included mark bits. For protected concrete bits, require a protected covering bit; do not consume new protected dependencies using ordinary coverage. Under a single equal header, maintain ordinary and protected antichains separately and combine their masks exactly. Preserve DAG sharing; memoization state includes the incoming ancestor coverage/mask, since one shared node can be reached under different prefixes.

Keep MAY and MUST separate in the first design. Current scalar TaintGroup has some cross-tail cells, but a MAY uncertainty assertion cannot establish a NORMAL uniform-taint witness. Normal-to-demand or MUST-to-MAY replacement needs an explicit operational/progress proof.

Two complementary canonicalization passes are possible:

1. **Inside the offered packet:** remove only strict descendants covered by an admitted ancestor in that same fixed header/mask stream.
2. **Across current packets:** subtract old coverage from the new packet, and subtract newly admitted broader coverage from old packets. Merge protection upgrades before deleting any geometry; invalidate/rebuild affected positional indexes without emitting fake kills or replaying old side effects.

These make the current spatial store independent of arrival order. They do not recover work already performed before the broader row arrived. More importantly, they do not by themselves prove invariance of the future query contract below.

## 2. Why MAY-prefix demand pruning is not currently justified

Take a late forward iteration, global limit at least two, matching full mark T, and empty exclusions:

```text
shallower demand Dc0 = x.[any]/T
longer demand    Dc1 = x.f.[any]/T
actual offered F    = x.f.g.$/T NORMAL

C2(Dc0,F) = x.f.*/T       DEMAND
C2(Dc1,F) = x.f.g.$/T     NORMAL
```

`Dc0` spatially contains `Dc1`, but C2 stops after the first new field. A concrete STAR initial has intrinsic DEMAND layer, while the concrete exact initial inherits genuine NORMAL support. Deleting `Dc1` loses both an exact initial and its normal lane. This is directly implied by `RestrictedInitialPolicy.kt:29–49` and `AdmittedInitial.kt:10–31`; the shallow/deeper-demand example is now validated by the external native C2 probe.

Even **inside-packet actual-fact minimization** can change C2 answers:

```text
Dc = x.[any]/FLOW
submitted packet = { x.[any]/FLOW, x.f.[any]/FLOW } DEMAND

before minimization:
  x.[any]/FLOW DEMAND
  x.f.*/FLOW   NORMAL    // intrinsic abstract-STAR entry policy

after keeping only the spatially covering root:
  x.[any]/FLOW DEMAND
```

`DemandStore.kt:145–152` visits every actual scalar leaf. `InitialDemandResults` deduplicates exact `(pattern,layer)` emissions; it does not spatially quotient them. There is an analogous issue for a MUST root plus a redundant MUST descendant. Thus extending spatial minimization everywhere without a query-level policy can remove useful progress that the current packed leak happened to preserve.

Existing cross-packet coverage already can discard such a descendant if the ancestor arrived earlier. The leak is not a promised refinement feature. But this arrival-order inconsistency is precisely why its removal needs a canonical data-versus-progress contract, rather than claiming every old emitted label was redundant.

## 3. Paired C5 coverage also includes the output budget

Use one fixed complete original `A = x.a.f.$/T`, which both rows can admit from `Dc = x.a.[any]/T`. Let current global limit be at least three:

```text
r0 = (Dc=x.a.[any]/T, Dp=y.b.[any]/T)      budget2
r1 = (Dc=x.a.[any]/T, Dp=y.b.c.[any]/T)    budget3
raw B = y.b.c.d.$/T NORMAL

C5(r0,A,B) = y.b.c.[any]/T DEMAND
C5(r1,A,B) = y.b.c.d.$/T   NORMAL
```

Although `Dp0` spatially contains `Dp1`, its shorter `FL(Dp)+1` budget cannot replace the precise row. See `DemandStore.kt:247–275` and `Reference.kt:224–254`. Initial normalization preimages must still use `canStoreInitial`, not simple spatial overlap.

A complete paired group must also retain correlation. This is invalid:

```text
r0 = (x.a.[any]/T, y.u.[any]/T)
r1 = (x.b.[any]/T, y.v.[any]/T)
claimed redundant = (x.a.[any]/T, y.v.[any]/T)
```

For `A=x.a.f.$/T` and `B=y.v.g.$/T`, r0 has the entry permission but fails the output, and r1 has the output but fails the entry. Their independent entry/output unions do not cover the claimed row. Every useful covering output must remain attached to a row whose entry admits this whole original.

The existing prepared plan correctly deduplicates identical `(fullExit,fieldBudget)` output programs **after** complete entry/member eligibility. This exact same-key work reduction is already implemented (`PreparedOutputPrograms.kt:95–119`). A broader group-reduction predicate must prove more than independent prefix unions.

## 4. Safe proof target for deleting a next-demand row

Fix next policy/view, method/direction, actual owner/entry/exit and complete runtime domain. For row d and retained group G, require:

```text
EntryEq:
  for every legal submitted packet F,
  C2(G,F) == C2(G union {d},F)
  as complete (canonical initial, intrinsic/support layer) sets.

PairedOutputEq:
  for every legal whole original A and raw output packet B,
  C5(G,A,B) == C5(G union {d},A,B)
  after native whole-pair checks, normalization preimages, stream packing,
  per-row min(global,FL(Dp)+1), layers, exclusions and protection.

ExecutionEq:
  retained native replay still performs required mark requests/Target effects,
  actual complete ND joins and input-alias closure; no ZERO/Target fabrication.

LoopEq:
  relation choice does not change growth-gate eligibility or exact consumer
  labels/results for a repeated/leave interface, unless that policy is
  explicitly redesigned and proved first.
```

Literal exact equality is the conservative optimization target. If the selected design instead wants a quotient by spatial denotation, it must state what replaces lost refinement/normal labels and how convergence/source permissions remain complete. That would be a design change, not a direct consequence of scalar cover.

`LoopEq` is not hypothetical: the new report has a fixed-premise NORMAL MUST short/long pair whose reverse results agree but whose growth tests differ. Deleting the longer reader changes whether a consumer query runs. The 456 captured classification-split candidates therefore require this extra check even before considering grouped demand pruning.

## 5. Practical next design candidates

1. Establish one explicit **data antichain** representation for same-header MAY/MUST memberships, including inside-packet and broad-after-narrow cases. Keep the native progress obligation separate; do not silently discard it when data geometry is compacted.
2. Initially preserve current refinement labels at the existing handoff/view boundary while testing a canonical spatial data view. This is a proposed proof interface, not authorization to add raw fact history or an unbounded new cache. A compact label is the paired entry/output pattern, actual owner/ports, mark/tail and budget/preimage policy, not the whole raw execution packet.
3. Reduce those labels only by `EntryEq + PairedOutputEq` (and complete execution/loop laws). Exact duplicates and equal output programs after eligibility are straightforward; root/descendant ANY patterns generally are not. A finite decision-program/trie equivalence check could factor a group without deleting its distinct image cells.
4. For NORMAL short versus DEMAND long rows, first prove the saved NORMAL relation supplies the missing concrete result **and** future source/Target/refinement permission for every relevant input. Spatial MUST-over-MAY coverage alone is insufficient. Keep MUST/MAY and NORMAL/DEMAND separate until that theorem exists.

The observed savings target is substantial (run-6 has 3,004 same-packet D-ANY descendant memberships; run-5 has 919/1,220 shorter-prefix MUST candidates), but those are inventory counts, not predicted runtime reduction. No proof here assigns every descendant to redundant execution, and no project experiment was performed. The bounded native controls validate only the stated C2 differences.
